1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 13 aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2631 Bighas and 04 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2004/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas land situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 25 of 2005-06 dated 06.02.2006 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioner is recorded owners/ co-bhumidars of the land bearing Khasra no.4//20(4-16), 21(4-16), 5//16(4-10) having 1/2th share LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Suresh Kumar
& Ors.

Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 13 situated in the revenue estate of Village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (as detailed in the Statement u/s 19 of LA Act) (in short,
the said land).
5. It is stated that the petitioners are the owner/co-bhumidar and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.

The said land is free from all sorts of encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.
6.

It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Suresh Kumar & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 06.02.2006, however,
physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment,
therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 13 development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,
which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after affixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Suresh Kumar & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 13 (vi)
The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2-3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to his village and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Suresh Kumar & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 13 police

(ix) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.

(x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with 30% solatium and interest @ 24% with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners are also claiming value of the trees admitted Rs. 1000 per quintal and compensation for the standing crops @ Rs. 1 lakh, compensation of tubewell @ Rs. 5 lakhs and the value of the room @ Rs. 2 lakhs per room alongwith other statutory benefits.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 i.e. UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the the petition is not maintainable as the petitioners have failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 13 in the present petition.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land in question prevailing at the time of issuance of notification under Section 4 of the LA Act.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to Ld.
LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 13

Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I LAC no. 242/2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 13 have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

sentences.text:
My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what extent.
15. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.

Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 13 18.

Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

19. In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) acquired through Award No. 25 of 2005-06 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs. 19,45,800/- per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/- per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre.
20. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioner shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

Suresh Kumar & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 13 in the present petition.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 13 18.
Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).

Therefore, the petitioner shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
22.
